scenarios.name: Switching from quantity to percentage mode leaves stale quantity values in submit payload
scenarios.oracle: After switching BOM mode from quantity to percentage, previously entered quantity values persist in form.bom[].quantity. The submit payload contains BOTH the stale quantity AND the new percentage for each row.
actions: Click '+ Add Ingredient' to add a BOM row
Select a component in the BOM row
Enter quantity '5' in the BOM row (bomMode is 'quantity')
Switch BOM mode from 'Quantity per unit' to 'Percentage'
Enter percentage '100' in the same BOM row
verify: Submit payload bom[0].quantity should be '5' (stale, NOT cleared)
Submit payload bom[0].percentage should be '100'
Submit payload bomMode should be 'percentage'
The quantity input is no longer visible in the UI, but the value persists in form state

scenarios.name: Switching from percentage to quantity mode leaves stale percentage values in submit payload
scenarios.oracle: After switching BOM mode from percentage to quantity, previously entered percentage values persist in form.bom[].percentage. The submit payload contains BOTH the new quantity AND the stale percentage for each row.
actions: Switch BOM mode from 'Quantity per unit' to 'Percentage'
Click '+ Add Ingredient' to add a BOM row
Select a component in the BOM row
Enter percentage '50' in the BOM row
Switch BOM mode from 'Percentage' to 'Quantity per unit'
Enter quantity '10' in the same BOM row
verify: Submit payload bom[0].percentage should be '50' (stale, NOT cleared)
Submit payload bom[0].quantity should be '10'
Submit payload bomMode should be 'quantity'
The percentage input is no longer visible in the UI, but the value persists in form state

scenarios.name: Double mode switch preserves original values: quantity -> percentage -> quantity shows original quantity
scenarios.oracle: Switching BOM mode away and back restores visibility of the original field values because they were never cleared from form state.
actions: Click '+ Add Ingredient' to add a BOM row
Select a component in the BOM row
Enter quantity '7.5' in the BOM row
Switch BOM mode back to 'Quantity per unit'
verify: After returning to quantity mode, the quantity input should display '7.5' (value was preserved in form state)
Submit payload bom[0].quantity should be '7.5'
Submit payload bomMode should be 'quantity'

scenarios.name: Creating a unit via dialog auto-selects it in the main form
scenarios.oracle: After successful unit creation, form.unitDefinitionId is set to the new unit's ID, the dialog closes, and dialog state resets to defaults.
actions: Select '+ Create new unit' from Unit dropdown
Verify dialog is open and fields are empty
verify: isUnitDialogOpen should be false (dialog closed)
unitName should be '' (reset)
unitSize should be '' (reset)
unitUom should be '' (reset)
unitError should be null (reset)
form.unitDefinitionId should be the newly created unit's ID
localUnits should contain the new unit appended to the original units array
The Unit select trigger should display the new unit's label

scenarios.name: Cancelling the unit dialog resets all dialog state without affecting the main form
scenarios.oracle: Closing the unit dialog (via cancel button or overlay) resets unitName, unitSize, unitUom, and unitError to their initial values. form.unitDefinitionId is unchanged.

setup.initialData: unit already selected in main form

actions: Select an existing unit from the Unit dropdown
Select '+ Create new unit' from Unit dropdown
Click Cancel button in the dialog
Verify dialog state and main form state
verify: isUnitDialogOpen should be false
unitName should be '' (reset on close)
unitSize should be '' (reset on close)
unitUom should be '' (reset on close)
unitError should be null (reset on close)
form.unitDefinitionId should still be the previously selected unit (unchanged)

scenarios.name: Dismissing unit dialog via overlay resets state identically to cancel button
scenarios.oracle: The onOpenChange handler resets all dialog fields when closing regardless of method — overlay click, Escape key, or cancel button produce identical cleanup.
actions: Select '+ Create new unit' from Unit dropdown
Close dialog via overlay click (or Escape key)
Reopen dialog by selecting '+ Create new unit' again
Verify all dialog fields are empty
verify: After reopening, unitName should be '' (not 'sack')
After reopening, unitSize should be '' (not '50')
After reopening, unitUom should be '' (not 'lb')
unitError should be null

scenarios.name: Unit creation error is cleared when dialog is closed and reopened
scenarios.oracle: unitError set by a failed unitMutation is cleared when the dialog closes (onOpenChange sets unitError to null). Reopening shows a clean dialog.
actions: Select '+ Create new unit' from Unit dropdown
Reopen dialog via '+ Create new unit'
verify: After the failed mutation, unitError should be a non-null error string
After closing and reopening, unitError should be null (cleared on close)
All dialog fields should be empty (unitName='', unitSize='', unitUom='')

scenarios.name: Creating a unit then selecting a different existing unit updates unitDefinitionId
scenarios.oracle: form.unitDefinitionId is overwritten when the user selects a different unit after auto-selection from dialog creation. The last selection wins.

setup.initialData: localUnits has at least 1 existing unit

actions: Select '+ Create new unit' from Unit dropdown
Verify form.unitDefinitionId is set to new unit ID
Select the original existing unit from the Unit dropdown
verify: form.unitDefinitionId should be the existing unit's ID (not the created unit)
Submit payload unitDefinitionId should be the existing unit's ID
localUnits should still contain both units (the created one is not removed)

scenarios.name: Adding then removing the only BOM row returns bom array to empty
scenarios.oracle: After adding a single BOM row and then removing it, form.bom should be an empty array. The BOM table should not render.
actions: Verify BOM table appears with 1 empty row
Click remove (X) button on the row
verify: After removal, fields array should be empty (length 0)
The BOM table should not be rendered (conditional on fields.length > 0)
Submit payload bom should be [] (empty array) or undefined
No BOM validation errors should exist

scenarios.name: Removing a middle BOM row shifts subsequent rows' indices correctly
scenarios.oracle: useFieldArray remove(index) shifts all subsequent rows down. After removing row 1 of 3, the old row 2 becomes the new row 1 with its values intact.

setup.initialData: availableComponents with at least 3 components (A, B, C)

actions: Add 3 BOM rows and select components A, B, C respectively
Remove the middle row (index 1, component B)
verify: After removal, form.bom should have 2 entries
form.bom[0].componentId should be A's ID, quantity '1'
form.bom[1].componentId should be C's ID, quantity '3' (was at index 2, now at index 1)
Submit payload bom should have exactly 2 rows with correct component-quantity pairs

scenarios.name: Selecting the same component in two BOM rows triggers duplicate validation on submit
scenarios.oracle: bomRefine detects duplicate componentIds and adds a 'Duplicate component' error at bom[1].componentId. The form does not submit.
actions: Click '+ Add Ingredient' twice to add 2 rows
Select the same component in both rows
Verify validation error on second row
verify: Form should NOT submit (handleSubmit rejects due to Zod errors)
A 'Duplicate component' error should appear on bom[1].componentId
bom[0].componentId should have no error (first occurrence is valid)
fetch should NOT have been called

scenarios.name: Submitting with an empty BOM row triggers componentId and quantity/percentage required errors
scenarios.oracle: An empty BOM row (componentId='', quantity=null, percentage=null) fails validation: componentId requires min(1), and bomRefine requires quantity (in quantity mode) or percentage (in percentage mode).
actions: Click '+ Add Ingredient' to add an empty row
Do NOT select a component or enter a quantity
Verify validation errors on the empty row
verify: Form should NOT submit
bom[0].componentId should show 'Component is required' error
bom[0].quantity should show 'Quantity is required' error
fetch should NOT have been called

scenarios.name: Percentage total recalculates when rows are added and removed
scenarios.oracle: PercentageTotal watches form.bom and recalculates the sum of parsed percentage values. Adding a row with null percentage adds 0. Removing a row subtracts its value.
actions: Add first BOM row, select component A, enter percentage '60'
Verify total shows '60.0%' in destructive color
Add second BOM row, select component B, enter percentage '40'
Verify total shows '100.0%' in muted-foreground color
Verify total shows '40.0%' in destructive color
verify: After first row with 60%: total = 60.0, text-destructive class applied, '(should be 100%)' shown
After second row with 40%: total = 100.0, text-muted-foreground class applied, no warning text
After removing first row: total = 40.0, text-destructive class applied, '(should be 100%)' shown

scenarios.name: Percentage total indicator is not rendered when bomMode is 'quantity'
scenarios.oracle: PercentageTotal only renders when bomMode === 'percentage' AND fields.length > 0. In quantity mode, even with BOM rows, the total is not shown.
actions: Select a component and enter quantity '10'
Verify no percentage total is rendered
Verify percentage total appears (shows '0.0%' since percentage field is null for the row)
verify: In quantity mode with rows: PercentageTotal should NOT be rendered
After switching to percentage mode with rows: PercentageTotal SHOULD be rendered
The total should be '0.0%' because the existing row's percentage is null (not yet filled in)

scenarios.name: Typing a novel category and selecting '+ Create' sets the exact trimmed string in the payload
scenarios.oracle: When the user types a novel category and selects the '+ Create' option, form.category is set to the trimmed input value. This string goes directly into the submit payload — no separate API call for category creation.
actions: Type 'New Mix' into the category combobox
Verify '+ Create "New Mix"' option appears in dropdown
verify: categoryItems should contain [...existingCategories, 'New Mix'] while typing
form.category should be 'New Mix' after selection
Submit payload category should be 'New Mix' (string, not null)

scenarios.name: Selecting a category then clearing it results in null in the submit payload
scenarios.oracle: The combobox onValueChange calls field.onChange(v || null). Clearing the selection passes empty string which becomes null. The nullableString transform in Zod also normalizes empty/null to null.
verify: After clearing, form.category should be null (not empty string)
Submit payload category should be null

scenarios.name: formError from a failed submission is cleared when the user resubmits
scenarios.oracle: mutation.onMutate sets formError to null before each mutation attempt. A visible error from a previous failure disappears as soon as the form is resubmitted.

setup.initialData: API returns 500 on first call, 200 on second

actions: Verify formError is displayed with error message
Click submit button again (API returns success)
Verify formError is cleared before the request is sent
verify: After first failure: formError should be a non-null error string, rendered as FieldError below the form
On second submit (onMutate): formError should be set to null immediately, before the API call resolves
The error message should disappear from the UI

scenarios.name: Submit button is disabled while mutation is pending and shows loading text
scenarios.oracle: The submit button's disabled prop is bound to mutation.isPending. While the API call is in flight, the button text changes to 'Creating...' (create mode) or 'Saving...' (edit mode) and the button is not clickable.
actions: Verify button state while mutation is pending
Verify button state returns to normal (if navigation hasn't occurred)
verify: While pending: button should be disabled
While pending: button text should be 'Creating...' (create mode)
The form's onSubmit handler has a guard: if (!mutation.isPending) mutation.mutate(data) — duplicate clicks are prevented

scenarios.name: Unit Create button is disabled until all three dialog fields are valid
scenarios.oracle: The Create button is disabled when: unitMutation.isPending OR !unitName.trim() OR !POSITIVE_NUMBER_RE.test(unitSize.trim()) OR !unitUom. All three conditions must pass for the button to be enabled.
actions: Verify Create button is disabled (all fields empty)
Enter unit name 'bag' — verify still disabled (size and uom missing)
Enter unit size '25' — verify still disabled (uom missing)
Select UOM 'kg' — verify Create button is now enabled
Clear unit name to '' — verify button is disabled again
Re-enter unit name 'bag' — verify button is enabled
verify: Button disabled when: unitName='' (trimmed empty)
Button disabled when: unitSize='' or unitSize='abc' (fails POSITIVE_NUMBER_RE)
Button disabled when: unitUom=''
Button enabled when all three are valid: unitName.trim() truthy, unitSize matches /^\d+\.?\d*$/, unitUom truthy

scenarios.name: Entering non-numeric text in unit size shows inline validation error
scenarios.oracle: unitSizeInvalid is derived: unitSize.trim() !== '' && !POSITIVE_NUMBER_RE.test(unitSize.trim()). When true, the field shows data-invalid and a 'Must be a positive number' FieldError.
actions: Verify unitSizeInvalid is true and error is shown
Verify unitSizeInvalid is false and error is gone
Verify unitSizeInvalid is true again (negative numbers fail regex)
verify: unitSize='abc': unitSizeInvalid=true, 'Must be a positive number' shown, aria-invalid=true
unitSize='25': unitSizeInvalid=false, no error shown
unitSize='-5': unitSizeInvalid=true (regex requires digits only, no minus sign)
unitSize='': unitSizeInvalid=false (empty string bypasses the invalid check)

scenarios.name: In edit mode, unit is displayed as read-only text, not a select dropdown
scenarios.oracle:
When initialData is provided (edit mode), the unit field renders as a

tag with the unit name/size/uom, NOT as a Select component. unitDefinitionId is not part of the update schema.
actions: Render the form in edit mode with initialData
Verify unit field is displayed as static text
Verify no Select dropdown is rendered for unit
verify: Unit field should display 'bag (25 kg)' as plain text
No Select component should be rendered for unit
Submit payload should NOT contain unitDefinitionId (omitted from updateItemSchema)
Submit payload should NOT contain itemType (omitted from updateItemSchema)

scenarios.name: BOM editor section does not render when itemType is 'material'
scenarios.oracle: The BOM section is conditionally rendered: {itemType === 'product' && availableComponents && (...)}. For materials, the entire BOM fieldset is absent. bomMode and bom fields exist in form state but are not visible.
actions: Verify BOM section is not rendered
verify: No 'Recipe / Bill of Materials' fieldset should be in the DOM
No '+ Add Ingredient' button should exist
Submit payload should have bomMode='quantity' (default) and bom=[] (default)
Form submits successfully without BOM

scenarios.name: Blurring an empty Name field triggers validation error, typing clears it
scenarios.oracle: Form uses mode:'onBlur'. When name is empty and the field loses focus, the 'Name is required' error (from z.string().min(1)) appears. Entering a value and blurring again clears the error.
actions: Leave it empty and blur the field
verify: After blur with empty value: fieldState.invalid=true, error message 'Name is required' rendered
After typing 'Test Product' and blur: fieldState.invalid=false, error message removed
aria-invalid on the input reflects the current validation state

scenarios.name: Create form initializes all fields with correct defaults, preventing undefined Zod errors

Optional fields (sku, category, description, prices) are undefined (not listed in defaults) and handled by nullableString transform.

form.bomMode default is 'quantity' — no validation issue
form.bom default is [] — no BOM validation since array is empty
Optional fields (sku, category, description, prices) should NOT cause errors (undefined is accepted by nullableString)

verify: name input value should be 'Concrete Mix'
sku input value should be 'CM-001'
category combobox value should be 'Mixes'
description textarea value should be 'Standard mix'

scenarios.name: Adding a new BOM row after switching modes creates a row with both quantity and percentage null
scenarios.oracle: The append call always produces {componentId: '', quantity: null, percentage: null} regardless of current bomMode. New rows have no stale data — only existing rows carry stale values from the previous mode.
actions: Add a BOM row, select component A, enter quantity '5'
Add a second BOM row (new, after mode switch)
Verify the new row's field values
Select component B in the new row, enter percentage '40'
verify: New row (index 1) should have componentId='', quantity=null, percentage=null at creation
Old row (index 0) should have stale quantity='5', percentage=null (not yet filled)
Submit payload bom[0]: componentId=A, quantity='5' (stale), percentage=whatever was entered
Submit payload bom[1]: componentId=B, quantity=null (clean), percentage='40'

scenarios.name: bomRefine validates only the active mode's field, ignoring the inactive field
scenarios.oracle: bomRefine checks: if bomMode==='quantity' && !row.quantity -> error. if bomMode==='percentage' && !row.percentage -> error. It does NOT validate the inactive field. A row with quantity=null but percentage='50' is valid in percentage mode.
actions: Add a BOM row, select a component
Do NOT enter any quantity value (quantity remains null)
verify: Form should submit successfully (no validation error)
bom[0].quantity is null — bomRefine does NOT check it because bomMode is 'percentage'
bom[0].percentage is '100' — passes the 'Percentage is required' check
Submit payload bom[0] contains {componentId, quantity: null, percentage: '100'}

scenarios.name: Complete product creation with unit creation, category creation, and BOM in quantity mode
scenarios.oracle: End-to-end create flow: create unit via dialog (auto-selects), create category via combobox, add BOM rows with quantities. The final submit payload contains all correctly assembled data.

Submit payload category should be 'Blends'

Submit payload itemType should be 'product'
Submit payload defaultPurchasePrice should be '50'
Submit payload defaultSellingPrice should be '100'
Submit payload stock should be '0'
Submit payload safetyStock should be '5'
Submit payload bomMode should be 'quantity'
Submit payload bom should have 2 entries with correct componentIds and quantities

scenarios.name: Optional text fields submitted as empty strings are normalized to null by Zod
scenarios.oracle: The nullableString transform: (v) => (v != null ? v.trim() || null : null). Empty strings and whitespace-only strings become null. This applies to sku, category, description, defaultPurchasePrice, defaultSellingPrice.
actions: Leave purchase price and selling price untouched (undefined)
verify: After Zod transform, sku should be null (whitespace trimmed to empty, then to null)
After Zod transform, description should be null (empty string to null)
After Zod transform, defaultPurchasePrice should be null (undefined -> null via nullable())
After Zod transform, defaultSellingPrice should be null (undefined -> null via nullable())
Submit payload should have all optional fields as null, not empty strings

scenarios.name: Entering a negative stock value triggers validation error on submit
scenarios.oracle: The stock field has a refine: Number(v) must be >= 0 and not NaN. A negative value fails with 'Must be a non-negative number'.
actions: Verify validation error on stock field
verify: With stock='-5': form should NOT submit, stock field shows 'Must be a non-negative number'
With stock='0': stock validation passes (0 is a valid non-negative number)
Note: '0' is accepted correctly because the refine uses Number(v) >= 0, not a truthiness check
